newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Father of racing ace Berger on trial for fraud.
newsitem.headline: Father of racing ace Berger on trial for fraud.

text.p: As Peter Graf was sentenced in Germany for tax evasion, another father of a top sporting personality, Formula One racer Gerhard Berger, went on trial in Austria on Friday for fraud.
Johann Berger, 62, stands accused of swindling a German bank out of 15 million marks ($9.2 million). He denies the charge.
Tennis star Steffi Graf's father was jailed by a court in Mannheim on Friday to three years and nine months for evading taxes on his daughter's income.

Prosecutors told the Innsbruck court that Johann Berger was in league with a Swiss-born Italian who tricked the Landesgirokasse in Stuttgart out of the sum on the pretext of setting up a wood plant in southern Germany, state television said.
The trial of Berger, who runs a transport firm in Austria's western state Tyrol, has been scheduled to last 29 days with a verdict not expected before mid-March.
The father of Austria's motor-racing ace was initially taken into custody in Germany in August 1994 and was released six months later on bail and on condition he would not leave Germany.
But in August 1995 he fled to Austria. His trial the following month failed as he refused to return to Germany. ($1=1.6383 Mark)
